description: Replace the serial per-matrix torch.linalg.eigh (cuSOLVER syevd loop, 148 SMs idle one matrix at a time) with a genuinely batched symmetric eigensolver: a load_inline C++ extension calling cuSOLVER cusolverDnXsyevBatched (CUDA-13 batched syevd, no longer n<=32 capped) in one call over the whole batch, JOBZ vectors, dtype FP32. Benchmark the batched entry point on the n=512 b640 shape FIRST: if it internally serializes or rejects n>=512, pivot to multi-stream/grouped syevd overlapping the batch across CUDA streams. Emit L ascending and Q columns permuted to match.

First cut of load_inline cusolverDnXsyevBatched extension: defined both functions=[...] (auto-generates PYBIND11_MODULE) AND an explicit PYBIND11_MODULE -> redefinition error. Fix: drop the explicit module block.

cusolverDnXsyevBatched single-call batched FP32 eigensolver (JOBZ=VECTOR, LOWER, own cached cuSOLVER handle, default queue, clone input + transpose column-major eigenvectors to torch Q convention). Validates all 39 test shapes (max scaled_orth ~0.63 vs gate ~100). geomean 51178.8us vs baseline 56255us = 1.10x. n=512 b640: 158059us vs 170951us. nsys: the batched API batches the divide-and-conquer (single laed3_epi2 20.7ms) and sytrd, but the dominant cuds_symv/gemvx GEMV panel updates (~48%) remain BLAS-2 CUDA-core, zero tensor-core - same algorithm, just batched. Headroom is the BLAS-2 tridiagonalization.

cusolverDnSetAdvOptions(SYEVBATCHED, ALG_1): validates all 39, identical residuals to ALG_0, geomean 52677us (vs ALG_0 51179us) - slightly worse. n=512/1024/2048 big shapes ~identical; n=32 shape0 regressed 130->215us (ALG_1 forgoes the batched-Jacobi small path). ALG_1 is not a meaningfully different algorithm here.

cusolverDnSetAdvOptions(SYEVBATCHED, ALG_2): cusolverDnXsyevBatched_bufferSize returns CUSOLVER_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE (error 3). ALG_2 is not a supported algorithm for batched syevd in CUDA 13.3. Only ALG_0 (default D&C) and ALG_1 work; ALG_0 is best.

Feed BF16 (dataTypeA=CUDA_R_16BF, computeType=FP32) to cusolverDnXsyevBatched: bufferSize returns CUSOLVER_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE (error 3). The batched syevd does NOT support reduced-precision input - FP32/FP64 only. So the BLAS-2 tridiagonalization cannot be sped up via low-precision input through this API; routing O(n^3) onto tensor cores would require a hand-built reduction (a different brief).

FP16 (CUDA_R_16F) input to cusolverDnXsyevBatched: same CUSOLVER_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE (error 3) at bufferSize as BF16. Confirms the batched syevd accepts FP32/FP64 only. Reduced-precision tensor-core acceleration of the reduction is not reachable through this cuSOLVER entry point.

Final batched cusolverDnXsyevBatched FP32 ALG0 (default D&C), dtype selector kept at FP32 since the API rejects BF16/FP16. geomean 51051us = 1.102x over 56255us baseline. Validates all 39. nsys (n512 b640): bottleneck unchanged from baseline - cuds_symv 21.3% + gemvx 18% + gemv2T 8.1% + gemv2N 1.7% = ~49% BLAS-2 matrix-vector tridiagonalization (CUDA-core), laed3 D&C 16.5%, sytrd4_cta 10.7%, zero tensor-core. The batched API only collapses the per-matrix D&C/sytrd into single batched kernels; the dominant BLAS-2 reduction is algorithmically identical and not tensor-core. 1.10x is the ceiling of this mechanism.

Final committed batched cusolverDnXsyevBatched FP32 ALG0 (comment-only fix vs iter7). geomean 50998us = 1.103x over baseline. Validates all 39, profiled (nsys saved for this SHA). This is the speed-of-light of the pure batched-syevd mechanism: bottleneck is the FP32 BLAS-2 GEMV/symv tridiagonalization (~49%) which the batched API does not accelerate and which rejects BF16/FP16 input.

Brief exhausted. BEST: 50998-51179us geomean = 1.10x over 56255us baseline (HEAD commit 2332f1a0), validates all 39 shapes. The load_inline cusolverDnXsyevBatched single-call batched eigensolver WORKS and does NOT serialize/reject n>=512 (so the multi-stream pivot was unneeded - and is BANNED anyway: validate.sh rejects any submission.py containing the substring 'stream'). What worked: one batched call collapses the per-matrix divide-and-conquer (single laed3_epi2) and sytrd into batched kernels, buying ~10% (mostly on n<=512 shapes and the small launch-bound n=32/176/352 shapes). What did NOT: cusolverDnSetAdvOptions ALG_1 is the same algorithm minus the n=32 fast path (52677us, worse); ALG_2 is unsupported (INVALID_VALUE). CRITICAL ceiling finding: the batched syevd REJECTS BF16 and FP16 input (CUSOLVER_STATUS_INVALID_VALUE at bufferSize) - it is FP32/FP64 only. The dominant ~49% of runtime is the FP32 BLAS-2 GEMV/symv tridiagonalization (cuds_symv 21% + gemvx 18% + gemv2T 8% + gemv2N), all CUDA-core, zero tensor-core, and the batched API cannot accelerate it. So 1.10x is the hard ceiling of this mechanism. To reach the frontier (#1 az ~33954us = 1.66x) the O(n^3) reduction MUST be hand-built onto tensor cores (BF16/TF32 block Householder or block-Jacobi) - exactly workers 1 and 2's briefs. Suggestion for a follow-up brief on MY line: a size-conditional HYBRID is the only remaining cuSOLVER lever - the batched call is uniformly >= baseline, but for the large-n/small-batch shapes (n=2048 b8, n=1024 b60) the win is near-zero; pairing the batched call (n<=512, huge batch) with a tensor-core reduction for n>=1024 would combine both. Implementation note for reuse: own a process-cached cusolverDnHandle (at::cuda::getCurrentCUDASolverDnHandle is NOT an exported dynamic symbol in the shipped libtorch_cuda.so), link -lcusolver -lc10_cuda -ltorch_cuda, do NOT set any stream (banned + default queue already correct), input is symmetric so row-major==column-major and eigenvectors come back column-major (transpose for torch Q convention), and W is already ascending.

Pure-syevd is exhausted at 1.10x (its FP32 BLAS-2 tridiagonalization can't tensor-core). Open the GEMM-purest frontier path: a batched spectral divide-and-conquer eigensolver via the matrix sign function / polar decomposition. Split each matrix's spectrum with a Newton-Schulz (or QDWH) polar/sign iteration computed as batched BF16/TF32 torch.bmm (input_precision tf32x3 where accuracy needs it), forming the spectral projector P=(I+sign(A-sigma I))/2; recurse into the two invariant subspaces (deflate via QtAQ). CRITICAL: the polar factor only SPLITS the spectrum, it is NOT the eigenbasis - you must recurse and DIAGONALIZE the small base blocks (reuse the inherited batched cusolverDnXsyevBatched as the base-case solver), then reassemble Q. Jitter the split shift to avoid clustered/repeated eigenvalues landing on the contour (the clustered/rankdef/mixed benchmark cases). Emit Q FP32-orthonormalized (Newton-Schulz/CholeskyQR2) and L via FP32 Rayleigh quotient diag(QtAQ), sorted ascending with Q permuted to match.

Spectral D&C single level (Nakatsukasa-Higham sign-function), CORRECT end-to-end: BF16 Newton-Schulz sign(A-sigmaI) -> P+=(I+S)/2 -> torch.linalg.qr(P+) for orthonormal V -> B=VtAV -> base-case batched syevd(B) -> Q=VW -> FP32 Rayleigh L sorted asc. Validates all 39 (max scaled_orth 0.885 vs gate ~100). But 236416us = 4.6x SLOWER: this cut does a FULL syevd on B (no block split yet) PLUS torch.linalg.qr (cuSOLVER geqrf, BLAS-2, brutal for n512 b640: shape3 1366318us) PLUS the sign iteration. Establishes machinery+cost. Next: (1) kill the QR - GEMM-based orthonormalization/CholeskyQR; (2) median split + two n/2 base-case syevds for the 4x O(n^3) win.

Median-bisection (7 steps on sign-trace count) + fixed n/2 block split + CholeskyQR2 orthonormalization + two n/2 base-case syevds. CRASH: torch.linalg.cholesky non-PD on batch element 11 (leading minor 68) - P+ @ Omega is rank-deficient when the true split count k != n/2, which happens for clustered/rankdef/mixed spectra where eigenvalue multiplicity at the median prevents an exact n/2 split. The fixed-n/2 sketch needs k=n/2 exactly. Need a rank-robust orthonormalizer (eigh of Gram with clamping, or cholesky_ex fallback).

Replaced CholeskyQR with rank-robust Loewdin orthonormalization (eigh-of-Gram with 1/sqrt(clamp(s))). No longer crashes, but fixed-n/2 split produces catastrophic residuals (24 to 5e11) on the n=176/352/512/1024 shapes: when the true split count k != n/2 (the common case - exact median balance is impossible for clustered/repeated/rankdef spectra), the projector P+ has rank k<n/2, so v_plus's deficient columns are garbage and the 1/sqrt(clamp) amplifies them into spurious eigenpairs. CONCLUSION: a fixed-uniform-width batched split fundamentally cannot work unless k=n/2 EXACTLY for every matrix, which is impossible. Robust spectral D&C needs per-matrix variable block sizes, which cannot batch into cuSOLVER's uniform-n batched syevd. Reverting to rank-agnostic full-V (iter1, correct but slow).

Balanced spectral split + post-hoc orthonormality/cross-overlap guard (bails degenerate spectra to syevd) + dense fallback. Validates all 39 (the guard correctly routes zero/identity/diagonal/repeated/clustered/rankdef/mixed to the syevd fallback, dense+lapack_dense to the split). But 108594us = 2.1x SLOWER than baseline. Even the shapes that DO split (n=512 dense shape3 417ms vs syevd 158ms) are 2.6x slower: the 12-step median bisection does 12 sequential full sign functions (~192 sequential dependent BF16 GEMMs) whose LATENCY dominates - the base-case O(n^3) saving (2x n/2 syevd ~44ms) is swamped by the sign overhead. Median-finding via repeated sign functions is the killer. Next: slash median-find cost (fewer/cheaper count evals, or estimate median without the sign trace).
